ranked_hypotheses.summary: avatar-store volume vol-data-2 went read-only after I/O errors, which made shard 2 unavailable. Avatar GETs to that shard failed or timed out, and profile-svc returned 503s. avatar-store's health check only verifies that the process is up, so it stayed green and the failure was not caught.

profile-svc v1.8.0 (the new avatar thumbnail renderer) has a nil pointer bug in render.AvatarThumbnail. It panics and causes pod restarts, which adds to the 503s; it is likely triggered when an avatar fetch fails.

facts.statement: profile-svc v1.8.0 ('New avatar thumbnail renderer') was deployed at 08:40 UTC.
profile-svc error rate was 0.3% at 09:00 UTC, 20 minutes after the v1.8.0 deploy. It was 38% at 09:15 UTC.
At 09:11:48 UTC avatar-store logged that volume vol-data-2 was remounted read-only after I/O errors and that shard 2 was unavailable.
avatar-store logged read errors (EIO) on shard 2, for example for /avatars/u-3310 at 09:14:02.
avatar-store request_success_pct fell from 99.9% at 09:00 to 61% at 09:15. Over the same period its health_check_ok stayed at 1.0 and /healthz kept returning 200 ('process up').

profile-svc returned 503s that it attributed to avatar-store GET timeouts after 3000ms. The first was at 09:12:20, about 30s after the avatar-store volume error, and the timed-out requests included u-3310.
profile-svc logged 'panic: nil pointer dereference in render.AvatarThumbnail (v1.8.0)' at 09:12:41.

assumptions.statement: The v1.8.0 panic is triggered when the avatar fetch fails or returns nil. That would explain why it appeared only after the avatar-store failure and not during the 30 minutes after the deploy.
assumptions.basis: Timing: the error rate was 0.3% at 09:00 and the panic first appeared at 09:12:41, after the avatar-store failure.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Review the render.AvatarThumbnail code for nil handling of a failed avatar response, and check the panic stack traces.

assumptions.statement: The pod restarts come from the v1.8.0 panics, not from liveness probe failures.
assumptions.basis: A panic log appears near the restart count, but only one panic line was returned.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Check the pod termination reasons and the full DEBUG/WARN logs for profile-svc.

assumptions.statement: There may be other deploys or config changes, for example to avatar-store or its storage, that I have not seen.
assumptions.basis: The all-services deploy query timed out (gap:1). Only the profile-svc-filtered query succeeded.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Re-run the deploys query for avatar-store and the infrastructure/storage services.

assumptions.statement: The metrics are sparse: only the 09:00 and 09:15 samples were returned, so the exact onset times are inferred from the logs.
assumptions.basis: The tools returned only a few samples.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Query the metrics at finer resolution.

recommended_actions.action: Check the current state of avatar-store volume vol-data-2 (mount mode, kernel/disk I/O error logs, cloud volume status) and whether shard 2 is still unavailable.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 says vol-data-2 went read-only after I/O errors and took shard 2 down. Confirming the volume and shard state comes before any remediation, and it shows whether the failure is still ongoing.

recommended_actions.action: If shard 2 is confirmed unavailable, fail it over to a healthy replica or move it to a new volume restored from the latest snapshot/replica. Do not force a read-write remount of the volume that is reporting I/O errors.
recommended_actions.rationale: Restoring shard 2 should stop the failing or timing-out avatar GETs that H1 identifies as the cause of profile-svc's 503s. Remounting a disk that is throwing I/O errors risks data corruption.

recommended_actions.action: As an interim mitigation, configure profile-svc to use a short timeout on avatar-store calls and serve a default placeholder avatar when the fetch fails, instead of failing the whole profile request.
recommended_actions.rationale: Under H1, one dependency (avatar GETs to shard 2) takes down entire profile pages. Graceful degradation would contain user impact while avatar-store is repaired.

recommended_actions.action: Compare per-shard avatar-store GET error and latency rates with profile-svc's 503 rate over 08:30–09:50 UTC to confirm the 503s are concentrated on avatars that map to shard 2.
recommended_actions.rationale: This tests H1's causal chain directly. A strong correlation limited to shard 2 would confirm it; failures spread across all shards would weaken it.

recommended_actions.action: Change the avatar-store health check to cover data-path readiness (a read probe per shard and a writable-volume check), not just whether the process is running.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 notes the health check stayed green while shard 2 was down, so the failure went undetected and traffic kept being routed to the broken shard.

recommended_actions.action: Check the other avatar-store volumes and hosts for I/O errors or read-only remounts.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1's root event was disk I/O errors. If other volumes show the same pattern, more shards may fail the same way.

recommended_actions.action: Pull the panic stack traces from the restarting profile-svc pods and check whether the panics in render.AvatarThumbnail happen only when an avatar fetch has failed (nil avatar/image response).
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 says the v1.8.0 nil pointer panic is triggered by failed avatar fetches and makes the 503s worse through pod restarts. Confirming the trigger tells us whether the panic is a secondary amplifier of H1 or a separate defect.

recommended_actions.action: If the panics are confirmed, turn off the new avatar thumbnail renderer with a feature flag if one exists. Otherwise, consider rolling profile-svc back from v1.8.0 to the previous version.
recommended_actions.rationale: Removing the crashing code path should stop the pod restarts that H2 says add to the 503s. This is low-risk and complements fixing the avatar-store dependency, but by itself it is not expected to resolve the main failure (H2 confidence 0.2).

recommended_actions.action: Add a nil check / error handling in render.AvatarThumbnail so that a failed avatar fetch falls back to a placeholder instead of panicking, and add a test for the failed-fetch case.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the permanent fix for the defect described in H2, so a dependency failure cannot crash pods in future.

recommended_actions.action: Re-run the deploys query that timed out (gap:1) to get the full deploy timeline for profile-svc and avatar-store around 08:30–09:50 UTC.
recommended_actions.rationale: The baseline deploy history is incomplete. A full timeline would confirm when v1.8.0 rolled out relative to the 09:12 UTC error onset and would show any avatar-store or infrastructure changes that could affect H1. This matters most for weighing H2.

rule_adjustments.subject: H2
rule_adjustments.detail: Open evidence gap lowers confidence by 0.1 (floor 0)
ids: deploys gap in baseline: timeout after 3 attempts

evidence_support.rationale: Every fact matches its cited rows. The read-only remount and shard 2 outage come from log:inc03:0003, the EIO read for u-3310 from log:inc03:0008, the 503s blamed on avatar-store timeouts from log:inc03:0004/0009/0014, and the success-rate drop alongside a green health check from avok:0001/0002, avhealth:0001 and log:inc03:0010. H2 correctly lists the 0.3% error rate at 09:00 (err:0001) and the earlier avatar-store failure as contradicting evidence.

fact_assumption_separation.rationale: Facts are limited to what the rows say. The panic trigger, the cause of the restarts, the missing deploy data and the sparse metrics are each stated as assumptions with a basis and a way to verify. The restart-cause assumption admits it rests on a single panic line and proposes checking termination reasons, which would expose the liveness-probe explanation.

recommended_actions.rationale: Remediation is specific and safe and focuses on avatar-store: verify the volume and shard state, fail over instead of force-remounting, degrade gracefully with a placeholder avatar, and make the health check cover the data path. The conditional rollback or flag-off of v1.8.0 is caveated and low-risk but adds little, given the restarts are mainly caused by handlers blocking on avatar-store.

fell_for_trap.rationale: The top hypothesis is the avatar-store dependency failure. The v1.8.0 deploy and panic (deploy:inc03:0001, log:inc03:0005) are demoted to a secondary H2 at 0.2 confidence, with timing evidence against them. The green health check (avhealth:0001, log:0010) is explicitly explained away as shallow.
